title: A Noetherian local algebra over a field, formally smooth for its maximal-ideal-adic topology, is geometrically regular
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $(C,\mathfrak m)$ a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring and $k\to C$ a ring homomorphism, making $C$ a $k$-algebra. If $C$ is formally smooth over $k$ for the $\mathfrak m$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], then $C$ is geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]: for every finite purely inseparable field extension $k'/k$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] the ring $k'\otimes_kC$ [def-weil-module-base-change] is a regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: More on Algebra, Theorem Tag 07EL (theorem-regular-fs, line 9872), implication (2) => (1) in both characteristics, and its proof (lines 9897-9910): in characteristic p > 0 by Lemma Tag 07EG (lemma-base-change-fs) and Lemma Tag 07EI (lemma-fs-implies-regular, line 9535); in characteristic 0 by Lemma 07EI alone (then k' = k)

proof.text: Fix any finite purely inseparable field extension $k\subseteq k_1$. Put $D=C\otimes_k k_1$ and $I=\mathfrak mD$. By [lem-weil-pbc-purely-inseparable-base-change-local-ring], $D$ is a Noetherian local ring with a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, and $\mathfrak n$ is the only prime containing $I$. In particular $I\subseteq\mathfrak n$. This applies also to the degree-one extension $k_1=k$; in characteristic zero this is the only finite purely inseparable extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension].

source.place: More on Algebra, Theorem Tag 07EL (theorem-regular-fs), proof of (2) implies (1), lines 9894–9907; the ideal-containment lifting argument spells out the topology change implicit there

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-base-change] to $k\to C$ and $k\to k_1$. It gives formal smoothness of $k_1\to D$ for the $I$-adic topology.

source.place: More on Algebra, Theorem Tag 07EL (theorem-regular-fs), proof of (2) implies (1), lines 9894–9907; the ideal-containment lifting argument spells out the topology change implicit there

proof.text: To obtain formal smoothness for the maximal-ideal topology, use [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] directly. Let $E$ be a commutative $k_1$-algebra, $J\subseteq E$ an ideal with $J^2=0$, and $g:D\to E/J$ a $k_1$-algebra map killing $\mathfrak n^q$ for some $q\ge1$. Since $I\subseteq\mathfrak n$, we have $I^q\subseteq\mathfrak n^q$, so $g(I^q)=0$. The $I$-adic lifting property from step 2 supplies a $k_1$-algebra map $f:D\to E$ lifting $g$, exactly as required by the definition for $\mathfrak n$. Also $f(\mathfrak n^q)\subseteq J$, hence $f(\mathfrak n^{2q})\subseteq J^2=0$, so the lift is continuous for the maximal-ideal-adic topology as well. Thus no unproved equality of adic topologies is needed.

source.place: More on Algebra, Theorem Tag 07EL (theorem-regular-fs), proof of (2) implies (1), lines 9894–9907; the ideal-containment lifting argument spells out the topology change implicit there

proof.text: The field $k_1$ and the Noetherian local $k_1$-algebra $(D,\mathfrak n)$ now satisfy every hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-field-regular-local], so $D$ is regular local. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], every prime localization of $D$ is regular local, hence $D$ is a regular ring.

source.place: More on Algebra, Theorem Tag 07EL (theorem-regular-fs), proof of (2) implies (1), lines 9894–9907; the ideal-containment lifting argument spells out the topology change implicit there

proof.text: The tensor product with reversed factors in the statement is canonically the same scalar extension: the maps $\tau:C\otimes_k k_1\to k_1\otimes_k C$, $c\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes c$, and $\sigma:a\otimes c\mapsto c\otimes a$ are ring homomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] (using the two structure maps in reversed order), and their composites are identities on pure tensors, hence identities. This ring isomorphism sends prime ideals bijectively to prime ideals and induces isomorphisms of their localizations; it preserves chains of prime ideals and minimal numbers of generators of maximal ideals. Thus the definition of regular local ring and regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] gives regularity of $k_1\otimes_k C$ from step 4. Since $k_1/k$ was arbitrary, this is geometric regularity over $k$ by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].
